Job Title
Senior Payments Specialist
Job Description
So, who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.
The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
Your role in the Team’s Success:
We are hiring a 12 month FTC on a full time basis, Hybrid in London.
This Senior Payments Specialist will be a senior individual contributor within the Payment Operations team, responsible for maintaining and improving payment processes, supporting audits and control assurance, and managing the performance metrics that measure operational health across payment operations.
The role combines deep payments subject matter expertise with a continuous-improvement mindset, ensuring payment journeys are accurate, efficient, well controlled and compliant, while acting as a trusted point of reference for colleagues across operations, technology, product, customer experience and risk.
What you’ll do
Process ownership, maintenance and improvement
• Maintain, document and continuously improve core payment processes across deposits, withdrawals, reconciliations, client verification and payment investigations.
• Identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks and points of client friction, and design and implement process improvements.
• Keep standard operating procedures, process maps and knowledge resources current, and provide operational guidance and second-line support to payment operations teams.
• Support the introduction of new payment methods, providers and products, ensuring processes are operationally ready ahead of launch.
Audit, controls and governance
• Support internal and external audits, assurance reviews and regulatory examinations, including preparing evidence, walkthroughs and control documentation.
• Own and operate key payment operations controls, and design and implement control enhancements arising from audit and risk findings.
• Ensure processes remain compliant with applicable regulatory, financial crime and internal policy requirements.
• Contribute to risk assessments and maintain a clear, well-evidenced control environment.
Performance metrics and reporting
• Define, track and report on key performance indicators and service levels across payment operations, such as processing times, success and failure rates, backlog levels, reconciliation breaks, cost per transaction and fraud losses.
• Build and maintain dashboards and management information that give clear visibility of operational performance.
• Analyse performance trends, identify areas of underperformance or emerging risk, and drive corrective action with the relevant teams.
• Provide regular, accurate performance reporting to operational leadership and wider stakeholders.
Fraud, risk and quality
• Monitor payment activity for fraud indicators and operational risk, and help strengthen preventative controls.
• Conduct quality and control reviews, ensuring transactions are processed accurately and in line with policy.
• Investigate operational incidents and errors, identify root causes and implement preventative measures.
Automation and transformation
• Identify and progress opportunities to automate manual activity and increase straight-through processing.
• Partner with technology and product teams on tooling, self-service and system improvements that improve efficiency and client outcomes.
Stakeholder management
• Work closely with customer experience, product, technology, finance, compliance, fraud and regional operations teams.
• Act as the operational point of contact for payment-related projects and initiatives.
• Translate operational needs into practical, well-controlled solutions.
What you’ll need for this role
• Substantial experience in payment operations within financial services or a comparable regulated environment.
• Strong knowledge of payment processes across deposits, withdrawals, reconciliations, verification and investigations.
• Demonstrable experience supporting audits and owning or remediating operational controls.
• Proven ability to define and manage performance metrics, with strong analytical and data skills and confidence working with reporting and business-intelligence tools.
• Track record of process improvement and, ideally, automation or transformation delivery.
• Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences.
• Methodical, detail-focused and able to balance business-as-usual delivery with change and improvement.
What success looks like
• Payment processes are well documented, efficient and continuously improving.
• Audits and control reviews are well supported, with findings remediated on time.
• Operational performance is clearly measured, reported and improving against agreed metrics.
• Fraud and operational risk are effectively controlled.
• Manual effort is reduced through automation and better tooling.
How we work
We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office.
Own the ambiguity: You'll work through it without a playbook, and get real ownership over how you solve it — excellence isn't optional here, it's the standard you hold yourself to.
Question everything: Curiosity is our currency — question what exists, and you'll have the platform to define what comes next.
Deliver at pace: The pace is real, but so is the momentum: deliver at speed, unpick hard problems, and help define the future of fintech.
Raise the bar: Take your craft seriously, and you'll be surrounded by people who take theirs just as seriously — that's the legacy you're building on, and adding to.
The perks
It really is more than a job. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships, volunteering opportunities, extra time off… the list goes on.

ICON is a global healthcare intelligence and clinical research organisation united by a mission to bring new medicines and treatments to patients faster.

• Direct experience supporting imaging studies and imaging biomarkers in MASH, obesity, diabetes, and other metabolic disease indications is required.
• Deep understanding of imaging biomarker development, quantitative image analysis, imaging endpoint strategy, and clinical trial design.
• Experience in applying advanced imaging technologies, image analysis methodologies, and emerging imaging techniques in metabolic disease research.

Carry out detailed fatigue and crack growth analysis using both first‑principles and industry recognised analysis/calculation methods
•
Analyse the life of rotating metallic (aluminium, steel and titanium) components consistent with Group A critical parts
•
Assess results against customer specifications and draw sound conclusions, including the generation of LCF, Damage Tolerance and Residual Fatigue

Determination of fatigue allowable stress levels for sizing

Determination of inspection intervals for structural parts consistent with CS25 requirements

Collaborate closely with Design, Test and Airworthiness teams to integrate F&DT solutions into the certification programmes

Author technical documentation to support regulatory submissions

Develop ideas and design solutions to practical challenges arising from new product design

Drive and manage test work that will validate the analysis

Support DFMEAs, other quality techniques and complete actions required to mitigate risks

Proven experience in evaluation of static and rotating components, specifically CS25 level lifing compliance with respect to LCF, Damage Tolerance and Residual Fatigue
•
Proven experience of Critical Parts lifing for LCF, Damage Tolerance and Residual Fatigue (Deterministic and Probabilistic)
•
Calculation of equivalent (Seq) stresses (fatigue and crack propagation), understanding of mission profiles, rainflow counting, Miner's rule and F&DT databases
•
Analysis of metallic and composite structures (Plain Strength checks, Buckling, Bolted joint analysis)

Knowledge of static and fatigue design values (Ftu, Fty, Fcy, AFI parameters, S-N curve parameters, fracture toughness, etc)

Practical knowledge of electric machines or rotating assemblies

Oracle Cloud ERP Finance Technical Consultant
Career level: Consultant / Associate Manager (CL9–CL8)  |  Location: London / Manchester / Edinburgh  |  Practice: Finance Reinvention Partner (Oracle)
Why this role
This role builds the Oracle Cloud finance solutions our clients run their books on. You'll take a finance design and turn it into a working, tested, migrated system that stands up at go-live and holds together afterwards. That means the configuration, the build specifications, the integrations and the data conversion behind them, and the evidence that it all works. You'll do it on large-scale Oracle Cloud ERP finance transformations, with real ownership of your own scope: a workstream lead sets the direction and owns the design authority, while you own the build within it and the technical decisions that come with it.
You'll do that work from inside the client's finance function, in their design sessions, alongside their controllers and their IT team. You'll explain why the system behaves the way it does to people who will never open a configuration screen, hold a design decision when it is challenged, and become the person a client comes back to when the answer has to be right. We're hiring for both halves of that: the technical depth, and the judgement to carry it in front of a client.
Accenture is a leading solutions and services company. Our strategy is to be the reinvention partner of choice for our clients and lead in the safe, widespread adoption of AI. We bring together our people, deep industry expertise and technology to deliver end-to-end outcomes for clients — and Finance is one of seven Reinvention Partners at the centre of that. Finance RP brings the CFO agenda to life for clients — stronger performance, sharper insight, and better control.
"Our clients want a partner that can help them reinvent—boldly, continuously and at speed… while continuously building the most client-focused, AI-enabled great place to work for our people—our Reinventors." — Julie Sweet, Chair and CEO
What you'll bring
Oracle Cloud configuration depth. Hands-on configuration of Oracle Cloud ERP Financials (Oracle Fusion Cloud Financials) across the core finance modules: General Ledger, Payables, Receivables, Fixed Assets, Cash Management, Tax and Intercompany, plus the enterprise and ledger structures underneath them. You configure it, you test it, and you can stand behind why it is set up the way it is. That extends into Oracle Subledger Accounting, where you understand how transactions are accounted and how to configure the rules that decide it; consolidation and close in FCCS; and enterprise data and chart-of-accounts structures in EDMCS. You stay on standard, extending Oracle the way it is designed to be extended rather than modifying it, and you can explain to a client why that boundary is worth holding. Experience across the wider Oracle finance estate, including the EPM suite and planning in EPBCS, broadens where you can work. The platform matters less than the rigour you bring, so comparable cloud finance platforms are worth talking to us about.
Design, build and integration. You translate finance requirements into functional designs and into build specifications a developer can work from, covering reports, interfaces, data conversions, extensions, workflow and integrations. You build the reporting yourself in BI Publisher, OTBI and Smart View, and you have worked hands-on with Oracle's integration patterns across Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) and REST and SOAP web services. Data migration and conversion sits with you, using FBDI and ADFdi, so a cutover holds. Where the standard product doesn't reach, you extend it properly, in a sandbox and through Visual Builder. You take the solution through testing and into deployment, and you know what evidence a client needs before they will sign it off.
Finance process knowledge. Genuine Record-to-Report depth, with a feel for how your configuration choices show up for the CFO: a faster close, numbers people trust, stronger control. You understand enterprise structures and chart-of-accounts design and the finance master data underneath them, how finance controls are built into the configuration rather than bolted on afterwards, and how those choices shape reporting downstream. Exposure to a second finance process area broadens your range.
Delivery and client skills. You own your scope and see it through. You make the configuration and design calls within it, document them, and explain them to the client and to the workstream lead without either needing to check your working line by line. You're at ease in front of a client: running a working session with finance and IT stakeholders, walking them through what you've built, taking the questions it raises, and turning a technical constraint into what it means for their close, their controls and their reporting. You are straight with people about what the system will and won't do, and you say so early, not late. You bring structured, analytical problem-solving and communicate clearly under pressure, and you support the people around you by reviewing a colleague's configuration, bringing someone newer through a build, and passing on what is worth reusing on the next programme.
Ways of working. We're increasingly an AI-first delivery team, bringing agentic tooling and orchestration into how we design, build, test and validate, with our people owning the judgement and the outcome. An appreciation of Oracle's own embedded Fusion AI and agents, and how they augment a finance solution, is a real plus, and we're keen to hear from people bringing that experience.
Who you are
You take ownership and follow through without being chased. You work well in a delivery team and build straightforward, trusted working relationships with client counterparts. You can explain a technical decision to someone who isn't technical: plainly, without talking down and without hiding behind the detail. You bring good judgement to ambiguous problems and you're careful and clear in how you make and explain technical decisions. You know which calls are yours and which belong to the workstream lead, and you raise the second kind early. You're precise about detail and thorough about proof. You test your own configuration and satisfy yourself it holds before you report it as complete.
Things that set strong candidates apart: Oracle certification; hands-on configuration experience on end-to-end Oracle Cloud ERP finance implementations, from early design through to go-live; depth in the Oracle finance suite, whether subledger accounting, consolidation (FCCS) or enterprise data (EDMCS); reporting build in BI Publisher or OTBI; integration and data-conversion experience on Oracle Cloud across Oracle Integration Cloud, REST and SOAP services and FBDI; an awareness of how controls, master data and staying on standard shape a finance solution; and a professional finance or accounting qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or…

Within Accenture, the Finance Reinvention Partner helps clients improve financial performance around the CFO agenda — driving best-in-class performance, and sharper insight and benchmarking across the enterprise. In the UK and Ireland, our Finance RP practice brings together finance strategy and the platforms it runs on, including SAP, Oracle, Workday and EPM.

It's a place to shape deep Oracle finance work and the offering around it, close to the CFO agenda it serves.

This is a lead role for an all-Oracle finance architect — someone who can stand in front of a client and take an entire Oracle finance engagement from design through delivery. You'll own the finance solution across the Oracle estate, set the standard others build to, grow the accounts you work on, and shape how we deliver platform-led Oracle finance transformation.
Accenture is a leading solutions and services company. Our strategy is to be the reinvention partner of choice for our clients and to lead in the safe, widespread adoption of AI. We bring together our people, deep industry expertise and technology to deliver end-to-end outcomes for clients — and Finance is one of seven Reinvention Partners at the centre of that. Finance RP brings the CFO agenda to life for clients — stronger performance, sharper insight, and better control.
"Our clients want a partner that can help them reinvent—boldly, continuously and at speed… while continuously building the most client-focused, AI-enabled great place to work for our people—our Reinventors." — Julie Sweet, Chair and CEO
What you'll bring
Your Oracle expertise. You know Oracle finance across the estate. Growing the work. You grow the accounts you work on — spotting where Oracle finance transformation can do more for the client, and helping turn that into work. You also help build the wider Oracle finance pipeline, shaping propositions and supporting new business beyond your own accounts.
Ways of working. We're increasingly an AI-first delivery team — bringing agentic tooling and orchestration into how we design, analyse and deliver, with our people owning the judgement and the outcome.
